src/rtsp.cpp (read 2026-11-03) defaults x-nv-general.featureFlags to 135 and x-ml-general.featureFlags to 0; the x-ml namespace is the Foundation fork extension, so a raw ANNOUNCE with only the standard x-nv fields is the upstream GameStream signature.
The pairing request carries only uniqueid, clientcert, clientname and salt. A device name is not a product identity, so no rule may fire.

src/rtsp.cpp reads x-ml-general.featureFlags and x-ml-audio.codec from more than one Foundation client family (Moonlight V+ desktop and Moonlight macOS Enhanced both document those features). Without a product token the family stays unknown.
An HTTP stack token such as okhttp identifies a library, not a product family. Guessing from it would violate the evidence-only rule.
